cards.text: The time is drawing near for David, king of Israel, to die, and he calls in his son Solomon for one last talk. David says, "I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man."

cards.question: Along with being strong, what else does David charge his son Solomon to do?
David tells Solomon to keep God's commands as written in the Law of Moses, so that he may ___ in all he does and wherever he turns.

cards.text: David says it's also so the LORD may fulfill a promise He made to David himself. No pressure, son, NONE at all.

cards.question: What did the LORD promise David?

answers.text: A man of his line on Israel's throne
A palace that would never fall
Peace with every nation around him

cards.question: True or false: The LORD's promise to David held no matter how David's descendants lived.

cards.text: Then the goodbye speech turns into a to-do list. David brings up Joab son of Zeruiah, and what Joab did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, two commanders of Israel's armies.

cards.question: What does David say Joab did to Abner and Amasa?
David says Joab stained his belt and sandals with the blood of war. Then he tells Solomon to act according to his wisdom. What should Solomon do about Joab?

answers.text: Not let him die in peace

cards.text: But not every name on the list is trouble. David tells Solomon to show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite.

cards.question: True or false: David wants Barzillai's sons to be among those who eat at Solomon's table.
David says Barzillai's sons stood by him when he ___ from Solomon's brother Absalom.

cards.text: My whole goodbye from the drawer fit on the back of one takeout menu, and David's has a SECOND PAGE. Next name: Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim.
Shimei called down bitter curses against David on the day David went to Mahanaim.

cards.question: True or false: When Shimei came down to meet David at the Jordan, David swore to him by the LORD never to put him to the sword.
About Shimei, David tells Solomon, "do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man." What does David want for Shimei's gray head?

answers.text: Brought down to Sheol in blood
Left to go down in peace

cards.text: And with that, the talk is over. David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

cards.question: True or false: David reigned over Israel for forty years, all of them in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was ___ established.

cards.text: That's David's last word and Solomon's first chapter. Stick with me, friend, because this story's not done.

findings.problem: Joab appears here for the first time but is only named 'Joab son of Zeruiah,' which doesn't say who he is. The baker isn't told he is David's own army commander (2 Samuel 8:16), and that is what gives David's charge about him its weight. Abner and Amasa are covered by 'two commanders of Israel's armies.' Joab needs a short tag of his own.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'heard' and 'learned' don't make sense in the sentence. Nobody 'learned from Solomon's brother Absalom' or 'heard from' him in a way that would make Barzillai's sons stand by David. That leaves 'fled' as the only answer that reads sensibly, so the card gives itself away. The wrong answers need to be believable actions David could have taken toward Absalom.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question quotes David's line 'do not hold him guiltless' as its setup. That line already rules out both wrong answers: 'Left to go down in peace' and 'Sent home to Bahurim' are what not holding him guilty would look like. Only the right answer is left standing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The closing line 'Stick with me, friend, because this story's not done.' copies the doc's example ('Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') with only the opening words swapped. The rule asks for an original line each time.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's humor is thin across the walkthrough. Only three cards try for a laugh: card 4 ('No pressure, son'), card 7 ('to-do list') and card 13 (the takeout menu). Cards 10, 14 and 17 are plain narration with no voice. Several moments could carry a respectful laugh without muddying a fact, such as Barzillai's sons getting a permanent seat at the king's table, or the shift from goodbye speech to instructions. As written, he reads like a pleasant narrator rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
